title: Dockside oncall logbook
content:
Dockside — Night handoff (Maya C.)

Quick summary (last 12h):
- Production fleet mostly green. Small blip at 03:40 UTC where 2 nodes in us-west-2 dropped pods during a kernel upgrade window (k8s preempted). Auto-recovered but caused ~200ms p50 spike and ~5% request 5xxs for 3m.
- Embedding pipeline latency steady; one outlier job failed when S3 had transient 503s (see JIRA INFRA-742).
- No customer-impacting incidents currently open.

Active issues to watch:
1) INFRA-742 (embedding ingest failure) — root cause appears transient S3 throttling; retry backfill scheduled, watch backfill progress and error rates.
2) kv-cache memory pressure on node pool "dedicated-pool-3" — OOMScore elevated after model-variant rollout; if OOMs increase, temporarily scale pool + drain oldest pods.
3) sporadic 5xx from proxy layer in us-west-2 — set of timeouts increased after recent envoy bump; rolling restart to previous envoy available as quick rollback.

Short checks (1–2 min each):
- API health: curl -sS https://api.redwood-inference.internal/health | jq .status  (expect "ok")
- Controller queue: kubectl -n infra get deployments | grep serving-controller  -> check READY/AVAILABLE
- KV cache memory: kubectl top pods -n serving --selector=app=kv-cache | sort -nr -k3 -- check top 3 pods > (norm ~2.1Gi)
- Recent 5xx: kubectl logs -n infra svc/proxy --since=10m | grep -E "5[0-9]{2}" | head -n 30

Immediate mitigation play snippets:
- If node preemption causes pod flapping (observed at 03:40):
  * kubectl cordon <node> && kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
  * Scale up pool: k ops (internal script) scale-pool --name dedicated-pool-3 --delta +2
  * If rollback envoy: kubectl -n infra set image deployment/proxy proxy=ghcr.io/redwood/proxy:v1.3.4 (previous stable)

KV-cache memory-pressure temporary procedure (fast):
- Symptoms: high RSS on kv-cache pods + repeated OOMKills in last 30m.
- Quick steps:
  1) kubectl -n serving get pods -l app=kv-cache -o wide -- note nodes
  2) kubectl -n serving exec -it <kv-pod> -- sh -c 'du -sh /var/kv/* | sort -h | tail -n 10' (identify largest keys)
  3) If a single model shard dominates, scale the kv-cache replica count down then back up to trigger rebalance: kubectl -n serving scale deploy/kv-cache --replicas=2; sleep 30; kubectl scale deploy/kv-cache --replicas=4
  4) As fallback, flip feature-flag: https://console.redwood.internal/flags?name=kv_prefix_caching -> turn off for the problematic model to reduce memory pressure (requires config-service restart).

Escalation contacts (quick):
- Primary SRE: Luca Rivera (Slack @luca.r) — mobile +1-415-555-0198
- Serving runtime lead: Arjun Patel (Slack @arjun) — pager if performance regressions > 2x p50 or persistent 5xx
- Product oncall (for customer-impact): Priya Nair (Slack @priya)

Emergency rollback checklist (minimal):
- Identify bad rollout (deployment annotation rollout.id)
- kubectl -n serving rollout undo deployment/<suspect> --to-revision=<prev>
- Monitor p50/p95 in Datadog for 10m; if regressions persist, escalate to runtime oncall.

Ops notes / small runbook fragments (to convert later):
- When doing a canary for model-variant, set traffic-split=5% and KV cache TTL=60s for 1h before increasing.
- For dedicated pools, prefer draining oldest pods on scaleDown instead of random to keep hot caches warm.
- Metric to watch for degraded decoder perf: tokens/sec per-gpu. Spike in tokens/sec with rising CPU indicates falling back to CPU path.

Commands I keep using (copyable):
- Check recent restarts: kubectl -n serving get pods -o custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,RS:.status.containerStatuses[*].restartCount --sort-by=.status.containerStatuses[0].restartCount | tail -n 20
- Tail proxy errors: kubectl -n infra logs -l app=proxy -f --since=5m | grep -v "healthcheck"
- Force a cache flush for model-x (dangerous): curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" https://internal-cache.redwood/api/v1/flush?model=model-x

Open items / follow-ups (write tickets):
- Convert the KV-cache quick-flush into a guarded API that requires approval + rate limit (ticket to product infra).
- Add a Datadog dashboard that surfaces node preemption events correlated with p50 spikes.
- Investigate why the rollout job for model-variant-12 didn't respect pod disruption budgets.

Notes to self (messy):
- Saturday's kernel-update cron probably too aggressive — talk to release-eng about window.
- Remember: when scaling kv-cache replicas down, some clients retry hard -> watch retries metric.
- If embedding backfill fails again, try reducing concurrency to 8 and enable exponential backoff in worker pool.

Closing handoff (for next oncall):
- Please check INFRA-742 progress and confirm backfill success.
- Keep an eye on dedicated-pool-3 memory metrics for 6 hours. If >3 OOMs in 1h, start emergency drain plan.
- If you see sustained 5xx >1% for >5m, ping Luca + Arjun even if you can mitigate.

Last quick log: 2026-03-12 22:58Z — validated envoy rollback image present in registry and can be applied immediately (tag v1.3.4).

——
Notes: this is a working scratchpad. Will refine into a formal runbook when time permits. Keep this file for quick notes; copy any durable steps into Confluence runbooks.
